proposals.evidence: Propose ordered four × ten. DEDR3655 and3918 explicitly give Tamil nāṟpatu/nāppatu, Malayalam nālpatu, Kannada nālvattu and Kota nālvat forty. Survey forms are comparative variants of these formations, preserving assimilation, reduced vowels and final vowels. No independent one-stem etymology is substituted for the two numeral components.

proposals.evidence: Ordered male + child components, comparing the contracted Tamil formation. Sri Lanka Educational Publications Department, Tamil11, printed p.112 (https://noolaham.net/project/795/79443/79443.pdf), visually verified, explicitly pairs āmpiḷai with āṇpiḷḷai in its colloquial/standard table. DEDR399 supplies āṇ male and4198 piḷḷai child. Survey contractions preserve these components; source vowel/rhotic variants remain unchanged, and borrowing versus shared formation across varieties is not resolved by this component analysis. See tamil-contracted-kinship-evidence.md.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 5160 directly groups the first-person singular forms in these languages. The source cognacy annotation explicitly identifies this article; full-article checking confirms the same pronoun family. Survey aēn and hēnu retain their differences from dictionary Kurukh ēn and Malto én; these are comparative proposals, not spelling corrections. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 3647 directly groups Brahui nan, Kannada nāvu, Kurukh nām, Malto nám, Tamil nām and Telugu manamu as the inclusive/general first-person plural series. The survey cognacy annotation identifies this article. The survey gloss remains simply we; no inclusive label is inserted into source data. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
